reason: The text contains no statement or implication that Yahweh doesn't owe loyalty to the people or considers replacing them with another people. Rather, the passage from 1 Samuel 14 consistently portrays Yahweh as actively saving and delivering Israel. Jonathan expresses confidence that Yahweh can save regardless of numbers (v. 6), and the narrative concludes with 'Yahweh saved Israel that day' (וַיּוֹשַׁע יְהוָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל). The entire episode demonstrates Yahweh's commitment to his people, not his disloyalty or desire to replace them.
